name: Earkart Limited
sector: Hearing devices, remote audiology and expanding healthcare services
summary: Earkart has demonstrated genuine hearing-care revenue growth, but weak cash conversion, margin dilution and post-IPO diversification prevent a compounder conclusion. BQS is 4.96 and capped GQS 5.00 for the verified parent core. IAS is NS because current group claims and revised deployment amounts remain unresolved. The funded core-only base diagnostic earns 6.86%, below the 15% hurdle, at the last observed ₹125.35 quote. This is a conditional deep review, not a completed whole-company fair-value estimate.

gates.reason: Disclosed promoter expense advances and control/compliance exceptions require dated remediation. Reported repayment and the unmodified opinion are contrary evidence; no substantiated severe integrity failure is inferred. [E14–E16]

Parent results and opening claims support bounded historical analysis. Original/restated and cash-flow classification differences are reconciled explicitly. Current group valuation evidence remains incomplete. [E07–E13][E17]

March free cash of ₹6.73 crore and authorized escrow fund core bear/base/bull cases. Severe stress needs ₹19.44 crore borrowing against the illustrative ₹8 crore envelope, so it receives no unfunded IRR. Expansion-halted 240-day and 300-day collection cases survive, the latter needing ₹6.91 crore debt. The stacked 365–450-day failures are remote boundaries rather than established credible operating conditions. Thus the gate is Conditional, not a false pass based on rescue and not a claim of current default. [E11][E12][E13][E20]

Sparse trading observations and a 1,000-share lot constrain implementation. The secondary observed-session median implies 32.1 capacity days at 5% participation for ₹5 lakh. Live spreads and bids are not verified; no suspension is inferred. [E21]

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Earkart has built a real hearing-device and remote-audiology business. Comparable revenue rose from ₹28.92 crore in FY23 to ₹54.04 crore in FY26, a 23.17% three-year CAGR. That growth is not yet high-quality compounding: FY26 PAT fell to ₹4.93 crore, operating cash was negative even after separating debt movements, and inventory, receivables and supplier advances absorbed substantial capital. The IPO improved liquidity, but raised equity is not cash earned from customers. [S1–S3]

The verified hearing-care parent earns BQS 4.96/10, displayed 5.0, and GQS 5.00/10 after the persistent weak-cash cap. Whole-company IAS is NS. The reason is specific: post-March foreign and pharmaceutical expansion, changed IPO uses and unreconciled deployment amounts prevent a reliable current group capital-and-claims bridge. Historical factors are still assessable; the omission is not a blanket refusal to analyze the business. [S7–S9]

At the last observed secondary close of ₹125.35 on 16 October 2026, a funded, five-year core-only base diagnostic reaches ₹174.66, or 6.86% annualized before investor taxes and execution costs, against a 15% hurdle. The bull reaches ₹447.83 with much stronger clinic economics; the bear reaches ₹44.75. These are conditional core boundaries, not a verified group fair value. Classification: mixed-quality research watchlist with insufficient evidence for whole-company investment attractiveness, not a compounder or an actionable purchase conclusion.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
As of 20 October 2026: Earkart Limited, BSE SME 544549 / EARKART, ISIN INE1A8F01035. The issuer-hosted BSE letter makes trading effective 3 October 2025. Figures are INR crore unless specified. Historical accounts follow Accounting Standards (AS) under Indian GAAP, not an assumed Ind AS lease framework; financial scope is the standalone parent. FY22 began on incorporation on 14 April 2021. The latest signed year is March 2026. No unreported H1 FY27 results or October cash balances are invented. [S1–S4][S12]

G1 Integrity: Conditional. The audit is unmodified and the company reports recovery of promoter-related expenses, but disclosed control and compliance exceptions need dated remediation. G2 Financial reliability: Conditional. The parent statements support explicit original/restated bridges and a claim-complete model; post-March group valuation remains incomplete. G3 Funding: Conditional. March free cash and authorized escrow fund the core bear/base/bull cases, while severe stress exceeds the illustrative bank envelope. G4 Tradability: Conditional. Sparse secondary observations and the 1,000-share lot constrain implementation; no suspension is inferred. [S1][S3][S7–S14]

Historical revenue inputs have High document confidence, while growth decomposition, governance, capital returns and core forecasting warrant Medium confidence. Whole-company valuation and live execution confidence are Low. Forecast uncertainty is not evidence that an audited historical figure is unreliable. The lowest material confidence governs the investment conclusion. The 19 October market session is the requested reference; ₹125.35 is only a 16 October last-observed secondary quote, not a verified 19 October trade or executable bid.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical primitive scores: GOV 4, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 6, EXEC 4 and EARN 4. No factor is assigned a neutral 5 merely because evidence is absent. REV uses the selected FY23–26 23.17% CAGR; the short relevant history and Medium economic-comparability confidence cap historical scores at 8. Other scores reflect the contrary evidence described below, rather than mechanically converting one ratio into business quality.

BQS = 0.20×4 + 0.20×5 + 0.12×8 + 0.10×6 + 0.12×5 + 0.10×2 + 0.08×6 + 0.08×4 = 4.96. GQS = 0.40×8 + 0.20×6 + 0.15×4 + 0.15×5 + 0.10×2 = 5.95 before caps. Persistent weak cash conversion, evidenced across FY24–26 rather than one isolated year, caps GQS at 5.00. Both composites have complete factor coverage. The displayed scores are half-up rounded to one decimal; the unrounded values are retained. [S1–S3]

IAS uses Q = exact final BQS 4.96 and L = 1. R, D and P remain NS because the current group perimeter and capital deployment are unresolved. Known weighted contribution is 0.25×4.96 + 0.10×1 = 1.34, coverage 35%, with framework bounds 1.99–7.84. There is no reweighting and no numeric IAS. The core base return alone would map to R2, but promoting it to the entire listed company would give false precision. Scores are structured research judgments, not statistically validated predictors of returns.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text:
Earkart combines hearing-aid distribution and manufacturing/assembly, rehabilitation products, remote audiology and a shop-in-shop clinic network. FY26 hearing-aid revenue was ₹41.23 crore, rehabilitation products ₹11.79 crore and services ₹0.51 crore; smaller parts and other-product lines complete the ₹54.04 crore total. Thus the reported business remains mainly product sales, not a recurring software or subscription model. OMNI remote-testing technology and clinic deployment can widen access, but service revenue is still small. [S1][S5]

Government customers generated 61.32% of FY26 revenue and private customers 38.68%. Uttar Pradesh represented 76.47% of invoiced revenue, partly because institutional procurement is concentrated there; that is not a measure of ultimate patient geography. FY25's government share of 69.32% uses product sales as its denominator, so it should not be directly subtracted from FY26's all-revenue share without that caveat. Tender prices are fixed and do not automatically pass through input costs. Performance guarantees tie up collateral and create contingent exposure. [S2][S5]

The June presentation reports 82 shop-in-shop clinics. The December call described ₹18,000–20,000 monthly realization per installation, a later ₹80,000 aspiration and about ₹2.7 lakh device deployment cost. The contribution split, partner economics, maintenance and mature-cohort cash returns are not independently audited. Subsidiary and pharmaceutical expansion confirmed in July broaden the business beyond this core; they are treated as separate capital uses, not silently attributed the parent's margins. [S6][S9]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Device certification, product development, OMNI intellectual property, institutional qualifications and a growing clinic footprint are genuine differentiators. They can reduce access costs and improve distribution reach. None alone establishes pricing power: tender awards are contestable, suppliers remain concentrated, and a remote clinic must still acquire patients and earn a return after partner and staffing costs. The FY26 margin decline is contrary evidence to assuming an already powerful franchise. [S1][S2][S5][S6]

In FY25 the largest customer represented 67.25% of sales, the top three 80.78% and the top ten 91.37%. The largest supplier represented 54.12% of purchases, the top three 73.98% and the top ten 84.84%. These exact historical concentrations are not asserted to be unchanged at the cutoff, but they make customer bargaining power and supply continuity central to the thesis. Private expansion must diversify both profits and cash collection, not simply increase the number of locations. [S2]

Osel is an imperfect domestic listed comparator because its LED/display activities differ materially. Sonova and Demant provide evidence of the broader industry's established brands, product development and distribution structures, not matched Indian SME valuation multiples. No peer P/E premium is imported. MOAT 5 means moderate differentiation with substantial uncertainty about durable excess returns; a higher score would require cohort retention, realized price/margin resilience and reduced concentration across a meaningful period.

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue history is ₹5.69 crore in the initial FY22 period, ₹28.92 crore in FY23, ₹31.75 crore in FY24, ₹43.11 crore in FY25 and ₹54.04 crore in FY26. Absolute annual additions after FY22 were ₹23.22 crore, ₹2.84 crore, ₹11.35 crore and ₹10.93 crore. The selected FY23–26 CAGR is 23.17%; FY26 growth was 25.35%. The first-year launch base would produce about 75.5% four-year CAGR, but is economically distorted and is not the scoring base. A five-year CAGR requires six year-end observations; five observations are not a five-year interval. [S2–S4]

The underlying volume/price/product-mix decomposition is not fully disclosed. Growth is consistent with broader hearing and rehabilitation sales plus clinic expansion, but no undocumented market-share gain or same-store growth rate is asserted. FY26 halves contributed ₹22.29 crore and ₹31.75 crore revenue, with PAT ₹1.85 crore and ₹3.08 crore respectively. This seasonality and institutional dispatch pattern make simple first-half annualization unreliable. There is no synthetic current TTM using an unreported half year. [S3]

The December call's roughly 25% revenue-growth aspiration was broadly achieved. Profit growth was not: PAT fell from restated ₹6.88 crore to ₹4.93 crore. The pipeline of clinics and private customers creates a possible runway, but scale alone is not proof of sustainable margin or cash economics. REV 8 recognizes the strong comparable growth band without an unsupported trajectory bonus or a long-history score.

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Revenue growth has required much more capital than the headline PAT suggests. A transparent financing-based invested-capital proxy rises from about ₹7.09 crore in FY23 to ₹43.34 crore in FY26, excluding available cash and the illiquid investment but retaining operating/restricted capital. Core NOPAT at an assumed normalized 26% tax rises from ₹1.08 crore to ₹5.69 crore. Incremental NOPAT divided by incremental capital is approximately 12.72%, around the explicitly assumed 12–16% nominal INR business-capital cost range, not convincingly above it. The latest-year incremental result is negative because capital rose while earnings fell. This proxy is not a fully acquisition-adjusted return on every project. [S1–S3]

At ₹2.7 lakh reported device deployment cost, a clinic's eventual return depends on realization, utilization, partner economics, maintenance and working capital, not installation count alone. The core base assumes 270 clinics by year five and ₹45,000 average monthly clinic revenue; the bull requires 500 and ₹75,000. These are research assumptions. The company previously aspired to 500 by end-2028, which is not treated as an executed commitment or guaranteed demand. [S5][S6]

The IPO's revised uses introduce a second reinvestment question. The approved summary table allocates ₹6 crore to acquisition and ₹2.5 crore to pharmaceutical manufacturing, whereas explanatory changes use different amounts. The model reserves the larger ₹8.5 crore project outlay, assigns no new-project earnings and no base terminal project value, and separately tests a ₹4.5 crore budget and recoveries. Until actual deployment, ownership and return evidence is reconciled, the new activities cannot justify a high DUR or CAP score. DUR 6 and CAP 5 acknowledge opportunity without equating opportunity to demonstrated cash returns. [S7–S9]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter/group ownership was 57.34% at March 2026; institutional or well-known ownership is not proof of governance quality. FY26 disclosed remuneration to Rohit and Monika Misra totals approximately ₹1.45 crore against ₹4.93 crore PAT. The IPO issued 3,315,000 new shares at ₹135, generating ₹44.75 crore gross company proceeds; the 334,000-share OFS generated seller proceeds, not company cash. The 825,236-share ESOP pool at ₹10 exercise creates potential dilution, but no options had been granted at March year-end. Full exercise in year five is a model assumption, not an assertion of existing vesting. [S1][S2][S10][S11]

The statutory opinion is unmodified. The audit nevertheless describes approximately ₹0.563 crore of selling-shareholder expenses temporarily funded from 8 October 2025 to 27 May 2026, with interest charged and a cheque deposited on 27 May subject to realization. Management states recovery. Subsequent bank realization was not independently located; this is not a statement that the amount remained unpaid at the cutoff. The model adds no separate recovery outside its mapped opening assets. [S1][S14]

The secretarial disclosures identify four UPSI entries not recorded in the structured database, cost records not maintained and delayed Form FC for the US subsidiary. The board describes corrective steps and explains the foreign filing delay by bank-account opening. Later closure is unverified. These observations do not establish insider trading, fraud or diversion. July's revised annual-report cover describes a clerical omission in the directors' report without changed financial statements. [S1][S14]

Execution is mixed: revenue growth broadly met guidance, but the June count of 82 clinics remained below the earlier 110 FY26 aspiration and PAT declined. A July AGM statement confirms UK and pharmaceutical expansion. The post-March perimeter, precise funding and revised IPO-use reconciliation are the key stewardship follow-ups, not speculation about management motives.

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text:
Profit streams must be kept separate. Original FY25 PAT was ₹6.640946 crore; the IPO restatement raised it to ₹6.881678 crore through disclosed expense, doubtful-debt, depreciation, gratuity and tax adjustments. Original FY24 and FY23 PAT were also restated. FY26 signed P&L uses restated comparatives, while its cash-flow comparator retains original figures. The latest FY26 PAT is ₹4.932301 crore under either comparison. Core EBIT excluding other income is ₹7.691199 crore and core EBITDA ₹8.351465 crore; a presentation EBITDA including other income is a different measure, not a contradiction. [S1–S3][S15]

Reported FY26 CFO is −₹12.562066 crore and includes −₹4.956853 crore borrowing repayment in its working-capital movements. Removing that financing flow gives −₹7.605213 crore operating cash on the research definition. It does not change total cash or reveal missing cash. FY24–26 reported CFO totals −₹12.848044 crore; financing-excluded CFO totals −₹11.636257 crore against restated PAT ₹14.872079 crore. Persistent weak conversion remains under either basis. FY26 capex was ₹5.369219 crore. Inventory rose ₹4.368 crore, net receivables ₹2.501 crore and supplier advances ₹3.507 crore. [S1–S3]

Net receivables were ₹21.069026 crore, including ₹3.586037 crore aged 6–12 months. The unit is crore after conversion from thousands, not ₹35.86 lakh. Average receivable days were about 133.9. Most balance confirmations were not received and GST balances remained subject to reconciliation in the disclosed notes; these limitations are not automatically a finding of misstatement. Tax-line labels and the deferred-tax-asset movement do not reconcile cleanly, so future normalized tax is assumed explicitly rather than inferred from a misleading effective rate. [S1][S3]

The model maps all ₹69.491891 crore of opening assets, ₹64.345184 crore equity and ₹5.146707 crore liabilities, allowing ₹0.000001 crore rounding. Cash ₹21.686738 crore separates into ₹6.733183 crore free, ₹14.126965 crore IPO escrow and ₹0.826590 crore current restricted deposits; another ₹1.126382 crore restricted deposit is noncurrent. Net operating WC is ₹37.372944 crore. Aged payables, current gratuity and current income tax are explicitly settled once; tax/interest credits recover once; long gratuity and refundable deposits remain terminal claims. Restricted money, tax assets, investments and guarantee exposure are not added twice. [S1][S3]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Market capitalization at the last observed ₹125.35 and 13,753,932 issued shares is ₹172.41 crore. Weighted-average EPS shares are not the current ownership denominator. The diagnostic horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with March balances explicitly used as a stale opening proxy. No undocumented interim receipts are assumed. Each annual row links government/private/clinic revenue, margins, depreciation, taxes, operating capital, capex, interest on average debt, escrow uses, legacy settlements, any equity rescue and terminal claims. Investor returns are nominal INR, pre-tax and before liquidity costs. [S1][S3][S13]

The base grows government sales 8% and private non-clinic sales 15% annually, ramps clinics to 270, raises EBITDA margin from 15% to 18%, and reduces receivable days from 145 to 135. It spends ₹8.5 crore on new projects without assuming their earnings. Escrow funds only permitted projects, incremental WC up to ₹5 crore and remaining SIS uses up to ₹0.626965 crore. Unused escrow and restricted deposits remain excluded from base exit value. All 825,236 options exercise at ₹10 in year five, raising shares to 14,579,168 with ₹0.825236 crore cash. [S1][S5–S8]

Base year-five revenue is ₹100.13 crore. At 14× normalized EBIT, operating value ₹233.02 crore plus free cash ₹21.97 crore, less ₹0.364596 crore retained legacy claims and no debt, gives ₹254.63 crore equity and ₹174.66 per share. Bear uses 9× and yields ₹44.75 / −18.62%; bull uses 18× and yields ₹447.83 / 29.00%. These multiples are scenario assumptions, not peer-derived fair-value conclusions. Core bear/base/bull remain funded without incremental credit. No dividends are assumed; terminal cash is credited once.

Growth/multiple sensitivity covers 8–28% growth and 10–18× EBIT. At 14×, the 15% hurdle requires about 23.23% annual core growth rather than the base's slower mix trajectory; 12% and 18% hurdles require 19.52% and 26.95%. The latter needs ₹8.91 crore debt, beyond the illustrative ₹8 crore limit. Removing future option dilution raises base return to 8.04%; recovering full project cost raises it to 7.56%. Neither rescues the base hurdle. The missing current group claims prevent R, D, P and IAS from being scored.

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A large tender loss combined with weak private monetization is the central operating risk. The ordinary bear reduces government sales 25% initially, grows private sales only 4%, uses 9–12% EBITDA margins and 190–170 receivable days, and writes down 10% of opening receivables and inventory. The impairment reduces recoverable opening WC, is charged once and added back once as noncash; replacement WC is then financed once. IPO/free cash still fund this bounded case, but its terminal price of ₹44.75 implies about 64% price loss and −18.62% annualized return. This is a scenario, not a prediction of an actual customer default.

Severe stress combines a 60% initial government-sales decline, shrinking private sales, 450-day initial collections, weaker margins, larger asset impairment, no tax-credit recovery and a full ₹0.79645 crore bank-guarantee call funded first from existing collateral. Required debt peaks at ₹19.44 crore, ₹11.44 crore beyond the illustrative ₹8 crore envelope. Although diagnostic later cash can repay debt, an entity unable to finance the earlier shortfall cannot reach that endpoint. No shareholder IRR is assigned to the unfunded path. An explicit equity-rescue alternative issues shares at a 40% discount with 2% fees and still produces roughly −32.4% annualized return; it is not an available financing promise. [S1–S3]

A different permanent-loss route is poor capital allocation: changed IPO uses, unrecovered acquisitions, additional group claims or sustained option/raise dilution can reduce per-share economics even if hearing revenue grows. Actual post-March subsidiary obligations remain unverified. A separate expansion-halted test retains 82 clinics, maintenance capex and all legacy claims, stops new-project spending, assumes a 40% government-sales shock and 20% opening receivable/inventory impairments, and keeps new-invoice collection delays separate from the opening write-off. At 240 initial receivable days it needs no new debt; at 300 it needs ₹6.91 crore, within the conditional ₹8 crore envelope. A 365-day version needs ₹14.52 crore and fails. However, whole-portfolio delays of 365–450 days plus multiple simultaneous impairments are extreme sensitivities, not established probable conditions: reported closing receivables are about 142 sales-days, the 6–12-month bucket is ₹3.586 crore, and gross balances older than one year are about ₹0.079 crore. G3 remains Conditional because credible restrained countercases survive, drawability is unverified and remote severe paths fail. The core stress cannot be used as a definitive bound on group loss. The thesis is falsified by enduring collections failure, uneconomic mature clinic cohorts or substantiated harmful deployment, not merely by a temporary share-price decline.

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A 5× price from ₹125.35 is ₹626.75; 10× is ₹1,253.50. Over five years those require about 38.0% and 58.5% annual shareholder returns. Even the favorable core bull yields only about 3.57×. The arithmetic therefore does not support calling this a probable 5× or 10× opportunity on existing evidence.

Keeping the base margin/capital structure and 14× terminal EBIT assumption, the linked reverse model needs approximately 51.13% annual core revenue growth and ₹426.01 crore year-five sales for 5×. It also needs ₹128.81 crore peak borrowing, far beyond the ₹8 crore illustrative envelope. For 10×, growth rises to 74.99%, year-five sales to ₹886.62 crore and required borrowing to ₹361.53 crore. These are algebraic, unfunded endpoints, not viable forecasts or assigned shareholder IRRs. Changing margins, capital intensity, dilution or exit multiples changes the answer; none can be assumed away.

A feasible exceptional outcome would require a much more cash-efficient clinic franchise, credible expansion without destroying per-share returns and verified new-project economics, not merely a larger addressable-market narrative. The model deliberately gives no unearned profit to the new pharmaceutical and foreign perimeter. It remains possible that those activities create value, but their current undisclosed claims and economics cannot support a quantified multibagger thesis.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
At the next primary interim results, reconcile collections against the FY26 ₹21.07 crore receivables baseline and approximately 133.9 average days. Warning: average days above 160 or the 6–12-month bucket growing beyond ₹3.586 crore without a credible timing explanation. Track inventory ₹10.92 crore and supplier advances ₹4.14 crore against sales and cash delivery, not merely PAT. Persistent replacement funding beyond credible cash facilities is a thesis break. [S1][S3]

Request a reconciled deployment statement for the ₹14.126965 crore March escrow and the May-approved changes, with actual ownership, expenditure, liabilities and remaining cash for each new subsidiary or acquisition. Check the next primary group balance sheet before assigning IAS. Compare actual clinic cohort collections, margins and maintenance with the model's 270-clinic / ₹45,000 year-five base; location count alone is insufficient. Confirm current issued shares, option grants and any new capital commitments. [S5–S10]

Governance checks are dated closure of the disclosed structured-database, cost-record and Form FC observations and evidence of the reported promoter-related recovery. Repeat findings matter more than promises. Before real implementation, verify primary BSE turnover, bid/ask depth, lot size and restrictions for the actual position. The ₹5 lakh illustration at 5% of observed-session median turnover needs about 32.1 sessions; at 2% it needs 80.3 and at 10% 16.1. Unknown missing dates are not silently zero-filled. These are review triggers, not automated monitoring or trading instructions. [S1][S12–S14]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
BQS 4.96 and capped GQS 5.00 place the verified core in a mixed-quality category, not the framework's high-quality compounder class. Revenue expansion and an emerging clinic proposition are real positives, but cash conversion, current capital returns, margin performance and execution do not meet the stronger standard. IAS is NS, not zero, because material group valuation inputs are missing. BQS/GQS comparisons are eligible within the stated core scope; IAS ranking is not.

Conditional action: retain as a research watchlist, not an investment candidate at this price on present evidence. The core base's 6.86% return is below the 15% hurdle and liquidity is weak. More bullish assumptions can create attractive arithmetic, but they must be earned through observable collections, mature-cohort economics and verified capital deployment. A nominally lower price would not by itself cure the unresolved group-claims bridge.

Reassessment requires current consolidated/perimeter information, reconciled IPO uses, funding availability, updated shares and primary market implementation evidence. Evidence of improved cash conversion and disciplined reinvestment could lift quality scores; repeated weak collections or destructive dilution could reduce them. This is a company-specific conditional research conclusion, not personalized allocation advice, a trade, or a finding of misconduct.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary evidence comprises the issuer annual report and revised signed filing, IPO prospectus, audited results, original FY22/FY25 accounts, investor presentation, earnings-call transcript, postal-ballot notice/outcome, AGM transcript/outcome, shareholding pattern and issuer-hosted listing approval. Important scanned financial tables were visually checked. The source ledger distinguishes directly read documents, partial tables and inaccessible filings. Secondary pricing and the September announcement index are not promoted to primary confirmation. [S1–S15][S19][S20]

The direct BSE September board-outcome download returned HTTP 403. Its secondary index describes a SkillNest proposal, but signed terms and completion were not verified; no acquired earnings are assumed. The issuer's July AGM transcript independently confirms UK and pharmaceutical expansion, so the perimeter issue does not depend only on that inaccessible filing. The revised IPO notice's allocation table and explanatory amounts require a later reconciliation. The exact current bank drawability, post-March cash, foreign/subsidiary claims and promoter-cheque realization remain material questions.

All forecast growth, margins, working-capital days, normal tax, funding rates, equity-rescue terms, future option exercise and exit multiples are analyst assumptions. The model is a bounded core diagnostic, not a consolidated valuation disguised by placeholders. March balances are not October verification. No DCF is asserted; sensitivities instead test growth, exit EBIT multiples and equity hurdles. No user-specific holding size is inferred from the ₹5 lakh liquidity reference. No public disclosure, brokerage action or outreach forms part of this research.

evidence.locator: IPO summary page 65; FY26 results page 6; FY22 P&L page 10.
evidence.limitation: Five annual observations do not constitute a five-year CAGR; FY22 is a start-up period.

evidence.value: FY23–26 selected revenue CAGR: 23.1718904407%.
evidence.locator: FY23–26 reported revenue, three year intervals.
evidence.limitation: The FY23 start avoids the distorted launch base; small size alone is not penalized.

evidence.value: FY26 government share: 61.32% of revenue. FY25 top customer: 67.25%, top three customers: 80.78%, largest supplier: 54.12%.
evidence.locator: IPO concentration disclosures pages 29–33 and presentation revenue split.
evidence.limitation: FY25 government share uses product sales, unlike the FY26 all-revenue denominator.

evidence.value: FY26 hearing aids ₹41.229937 crore, rehabilitation ₹11.793815 crore and services ₹0.511638 crore; 82 clinics in the June presentation.
evidence.locator: Annual note 14 and presentation business model.
evidence.limitation: Clinic-specific audited revenue and mature-cohort profitability are not disclosed.

evidence.value: December 2025 management: 56 clinics, 110 FY26 target, ₹18,000–20,000 monthly realization, ₹80,000 aspiration, ₹2.7 lakh device cost and 500 clinics by end-2028.
evidence.locator: December call clinic questions and answers.
evidence.limitation: Targets are not executed orders or audited unit returns.

evidence.value: FY26 PAT ₹4.932301 crore versus restated FY25 ₹6.881678 crore; FY26 core EBIT ₹7.691199 crore.
evidence.locator: Signed P&L and notes 14–22.
evidence.limitation: FY25 original PAT was ₹6.640946 crore; the restated comparison is stated explicitly.

evidence.value: FY25 original PAT ₹6.6409 crore plus ₹0.2407 crore adjustments equals restated ₹6.8817 crore. FY24 ₹3.2208 becomes ₹3.0581; FY23 ₹1.2849 becomes ₹1.3120 crore.
evidence.locator: IPO restatement pages 199–200.
evidence.limitation: The prospectus explains disclosed restatements; no new allegation of misconduct is made.

evidence.value: FY26 CFO −₹12.562066 crore includes −₹4.956853 crore borrowing repayment. Financing-excluded operating cash is −₹7.605213 crore.
evidence.locator: Signed cash-flow statement page 8, visually inspected.
evidence.limitation: Analytical classification changes operating/financing subtotals, not total cash.

evidence.value: FY24–26 reported CFO −₹12.848044 crore; financing-excluded CFO −₹11.636257 crore; restated PAT ₹14.872079 crore.
evidence.locator: IPO cash-flow summary page 66 and FY26 signed cash flow page 8.
evidence.limitation: Using original PAT of ₹14.794047 crore changes the ratio slightly but not the conclusion.

evidence.value: ₹21.686738 crore reported cash = ₹6.733183 crore free + ₹14.126965 crore escrow + ₹0.826590 crore restricted deposits. Additional noncurrent restricted deposits: ₹1.126382 crore.
evidence.locator: Annual notes 8.4 and 11, balance sheet.
evidence.limitation: IPO proceeds are usable for permitted objects, not generally fungible cash.

evidence.value: Mapped assets ₹69.491891 crore = equity ₹64.345184 crore + liabilities ₹5.146707 crore, allowing ₹0.000001 crore source rounding.
evidence.locator: Annual notes 3–13 and the complete opening-claim ledger.
evidence.limitation: Every opening asset/liability is mapped once. The ₹0.796450 crore guarantee is separate contingent exposure.

evidence.value: Net receivables ₹21.069026 crore, including ₹3.586037 crore aged 6–12 months; inventory ₹10.917629 crore; net operating WC ₹37.372944 crore.
evidence.locator: Annual receivable/inventory notes 9–10 and claim bridge.
evidence.limitation: The source unit is INR thousands. The 6–12-month receivable bucket is ₹3.586037 crore, not ₹35.86 lakh.

evidence.value: ₹0.563434 crore promoter-related expenses temporarily funded from 8 October 2025 to 27 May 2026. Auditor describes cheque deposit on 27 May subject to realization, with interest charged.
evidence.locator: CARO pages 44–47 and explanatory notes pages 64–67.
evidence.limitation: Later bank realization was not independently verified. No assertion of unpaid balance at the cutoff or fraud is made.

evidence.value: Four UPSI database entries not recorded, cost records not maintained and delayed Form FC. The board describes corrective measures and a bank-opening explanation.
evidence.locator: Directors report pages 92–93 and secretarial annexure.
evidence.limitation: Later remediation is unverified. These observations do not establish insider trading or fraud.

evidence.value: May-approved summary allocates ₹2.5 crore to pharma, ₹6 crore to acquisition and ₹5 crore additional WC. Explanatory variation amounts instead use ₹0.5 crore, ₹4 crore and ₹8.5469 crore.
evidence.locator: Postal resolution, allocation table, explanatory statement and voting outcome.
evidence.limitation: A later reconciled deployment statement is required. No unauthorized use or acquisition completion is inferred.

evidence.value: US subsidiary incorporated January 2026. July AGM confirms UK subsidiary in June and pharma launch in July. September education proposal appears only in the retrieved secondary index.
evidence.locator: Annual subsidiary note 13, July AGM remarks and September index.
evidence.limitation: No audited post-March group ownership, funding and claims bridge was retrieved. The September primary PDF returned HTTP 403.

evidence.value: IPO: 3,315,000 fresh shares at ₹135; 334,000 OFS shares are not company proceeds. ESOP pool: 825,236 at ₹10 exercise, with no grants at March year-end.
evidence.locator: Share-capital note, directors ESOP disclosure and AGM materials.
evidence.limitation: Future full-pool exercise is an analyst scenario, not actual vesting.

evidence.value: FY23–26 invested-capital proxy: ₹7.0897 crore to ₹43.337852 crore. Normalized NOPAT: ₹1.07929 crore to ₹5.69148726 crore. Incremental return: 12.72395144%.
evidence.locator: Core P&L and explicit financing-based invested-capital calculation.
evidence.limitation: This is a transparent financing proxy, not fully acquisition-adjusted project ROIC. The latest annual incremental return is negative.
evidence.formula: (5.69148726 − 1.07929) / (43.337852 − 7.0897) = 0.12723951444. IC = equity + debt − available cash − illiquid investment; NOPAT = core EBIT × 0.74.

evidence.value: Core bear/base/bull annual returns: −18.62%, 6.86% and 29.00%. Severe required borrowing ₹19.44 crore exceeds the ₹8 crore envelope; no IRR is assigned to that unfunded path.
evidence.locator: Linked annual scenarios and funding/terminal bridges.
evidence.limitation: These are conditional core diagnostics, not whole-company expected returns.

evidence.value: Last observed quote ₹125.35 on 16 October. Observed dates: 24/60 and 6/20. Sixty-session observed median close-times-volume proxy: ₹311,500.
evidence.locator: Dated secondary OHLCV observations and observed-session liquidity windows.
evidence.limitation: Missing rows are not proven zero trades. Live spread/depth and primary BSE restrictions are unverified.

evidence.value: Osel has mixed LED/hearing activities; Sonova and Demant are international hearing-healthcare comparators, not matched valuation peers.
evidence.locator: IPO peer comparison and primary company business pages.
evidence.limitation: No matched peer valuation, premium or numerical quality ranking is asserted.

GOV.reason: Unmodified statutory opinion and reported repayment are positives. However, several disclosed control/compliance exceptions and rapid redeployment away from original IPO objects weaken stewardship confidence. Neither celebrity investors nor an audit opinion substitutes for remediation evidence.
GOV.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

MOAT.reason: Own devices, qualification, distribution and remote diagnostics offer useful differentiation. Concentrated tender sales, concentrated suppliers, contestable clinics and declining margins are contrary evidence against a durable pricing moat.
MOAT.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

REV.reason: The selected FY23–26 revenue CAGR is 23.17%, within the 20–30% band. FY26 growth was 25.35%. The launch year would distort growth; no trajectory bonus is applied, and relevant-history confidence caps the factor at 8.
REV.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

DUR.reason: Clinic access and rising private sales provide a real runway. Actual June footprint82 is far below the500target, unit economics remain immature and diversification is not an independently demonstrated extension of the hearing franchise.
DUR.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

CAP.reason: The FY23–26 incremental NOPAT/capital proxy is 12.72%, around an assumed 12–16% nominal INR capital-cost range. The latest incremental result is negative. Mature clinic returns have not yet demonstrated a persistent excess.
CAP.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

CASH.reason: Cash realization is persistently weak even after removing borrowings from reported CFO. Inventory, advances and ageing receivables absorb capital. IPO funding prevents this from being synonymous with insolvency, but does not turn raised equity into earned cash.
CASH.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

BAL.reason: March debt is negligible, with ₹6.73 crore free cash and ₹14.13 crore authorized escrow. Restricted deposits, a stale opening date, new-project obligations and a ₹19.44 crore severe borrowing need limit resilience.
BAL.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

EXEC.reason: FY26 revenue growth broadly met the December 25% aspiration. June clinics numbered 82 versus the earlier 110 FY26 target. Profit fell while scope expanded; cohort and new-project execution remain to be demonstrated.
EXEC.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

EARN.reason: Core operations produce most earnings, not other income. However, PAT fell versus both original and restated FY25, issued shares increased 31.76%, and tax/EPS presentation requires explicit reconciliation. Per-share compounding is not established.
EARN.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

R.reason: The core base return of 6.86% would map to R2 at a 15% hurdle. It cannot substitute for a current whole-company return without verified perimeter and capital deployment.
R.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

D.reason: Core bear and severe stress are quantified, including financing failure. Whole-company subsidiary/acquisition claims and recovery economics remain unverified, so the factor is NS.
D.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

P.reason: Core reverse expectations are calculable, but a current group attribution and valuation cannot be supported. The factor is NS rather than an invented midpoint.
P.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

L.reason: The observed-session median proxy implies 32.1 capacity days at 5% participation for ₹5 lakh, beyond the 20-day threshold. Lot rounding and sparse dates constrain execution; missing-date zero filling is only a separate sensitivity.
L.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

Q.reason: Exact unrounded final BQS of 4.96 is used once, not a new independent factor.
Q.history_basis: FY2023–FY2026 comparable core. No historical factor scores 9–10.

confidence.revenue_history: High for retrieved amounts; Medium for economic growth decomposition.
confidence.forecast_uncertainty: High uncertainty, distinct from confidence in historical documents.
confidence.liquidity: Medium for coarse observed-history analysis; Low for live execution.
confidence.overall: Low for the investment conclusion; Medium for the BQS/GQS core assessment.

limitations: March opening balances are not October cash verification. No post-March receipts are assumed except explicitly modeled recoveries.
The reported March PNB sanction is ₹8 crore. Drawability and renewal at the cutoff are not verified. A no-credit variant is supplied.
No dividends are assumed. The whole option pool exercises at ₹10 in year five only as a scenario, not as an actual grant or vesting claim.

Escrow budget follows the approved notice summary: acquisition ₹6 crore, pharma ₹2.5 crore, additional WC ₹5 crore and remaining SIS authorization ₹0.626965 crore. A conflicting ₹4.5 crore project-budget alternative is tested.
Core margins include operating rent and recurring payroll/benefit funding. The opening long-term benefit claim is retained at exit, with no lease-debt double count.
New projects generate no modeled earnings. Bull residual value of ₹4.25 crore and full-cost recovery of ₹8.5 crore are assumptions, not independently established valuations.
Tax labels do not reconcile cleanly with the deferred-tax-asset note. Normalized 26% and adverse 30–33% tax rates are model assumptions, not recovered historical cash tax.
Annual cash funding does not establish seasonal or monthly facility availability. The base has no incremental bank dependence, but severe stress fails the stated funding ceiling.

The smaller project-budget and isolated receivable-impairment variants can leave free terminal cash unchanged because escrow use adjusts. Unused escrow remains excluded, so this is not a claim that project losses have no economic cost.

valuation.lease_treatment: Operating rent is included in core margins under the reported AS basis. Disclosed minimum rent is ₹0.585 crore within one year and ₹0.63375 crore in years two and three; it is not added again as debt.
valuation.dividends: None assumed; retained cash is credited once at exit.

liquidity.zero_filled_sensitivity: If all 36 missing dates were true zero-trade sessions, the median would be zero and no finite exit-capacity estimate would result. This is a conditional sensitivity, not a finding about missing dates.

Original/restated results, cash-flow classification and tax/EPS presentation differ across documents. Explicit streams are retained. There is no inference of missing cash or fraud.

The last observed secondary quote is dated 16 October, not a verified 19 October trade or executable bid. Current BSE restrictions, live spreads and complete primary traded-value data are not established.

The core model uses 31 March balances as an explicit proxy at 19 October 2026. Option exercise, deployment timing, margins, normal tax and financing terms are assumptions. Annual funding does not establish intra-year cash availability.
Current customer/supplier concentration, clinic cohort profitability and a complete volume/price growth bridge are not disclosed. A three-year REV 8 does not establish a long-cycle moat.
